items.text: The execution tracking uses a pure polling model: swarm-manager polls agent-manager every 2 seconds via GET /api/v1/runs/{runID}. Agent-manager never pushes status back. Four bugs were identified in the codebase investigation.

agentactivity.Service wraps agentmanager.AgentService but does NOT forward the GetRunDiff method. This causes s.differ to always be nil in execution/service.go, meaning sandbox diffs are never fetched during finalization. If acceptance_allow is empty, finalization is skipped entirely.

items.context: agentactivity.Service wraps the raw agentmanager.AgentService but doesn't implement the RunDiffer interface. The type assertion in service.go NewService() fails silently, leaving s.differ as nil. We need to make the differ available to the execution service.

options.label: Add GetRunDiff forwarding to agentactivity.Service
options.rationale: Simplest fix — add a GetRunDiff method to agentactivity.Service that delegates to the inner agentmanager.AgentService. Preserves existing wiring, minimal code change.

options.label: Pass raw agentmanager.AgentService alongside agentactivity.Service
options.rationale: Wire both services into ServiceConfig separately — one for activity tracking, one for differ. More explicit but requires changing the config struct and call sites.

items.context: When agent-manager restarts or loses a run record, swarm-manager polls forever because errors from GetRunState are silently ignored (continue on err). Runs can be stuck in StatusStarting or StatusRunning indefinitely. Agent-manager has its own StaleThreshold of 5 minutes for heartbeats.

options.label: Configurable timeout with consecutive-error counter
options.rationale: Track consecutive poll errors per run. After N consecutive errors (e.g., 10 = 20 seconds of failures), mark the run as failed. Also add a max-age timeout (e.g., 30 min default). Handles both lost runs and hung runs.

options.label: Simple max-age timeout only
options.rationale: If a run has been in a non-terminal state for longer than a threshold (e.g., 30 min), mark it as failed. Simpler but doesn't catch lost runs quickly — could wait 30 min for a run that 404s immediately.

options.label: Treat 404 specifically as 'run lost'
options.rationale: Parse the HTTP status from GetRunState errors. On 404, immediately mark the run as failed. On other errors, continue polling. Does not handle hung runs that never complete.

items.notes: Default should be more than 20s. Restarting can sometimes take minutes

items.context: Currently mapRunStatus returns StatusRunning for any unrecognized status string, which means unknown statuses cause infinite polling. We need a safer default, but being too aggressive (immediate failure) could break forward compatibility if agent-manager adds new legitimate statuses.

options.label: Log warning and return StatusFailed after grace period
options.rationale: On first unknown status, log a warning and keep StatusRunning. Track how many consecutive polls returned an unknown status. After a threshold (e.g., 5 polls = 10 seconds), transition to StatusFailed. Balances safety with forward compatibility.

options.label: Immediately return a new StatusUnknown terminal state
options.rationale: Add a StatusUnknown that is terminal — stops polling immediately. Clean but could prematurely kill runs if agent-manager adds a legitimate new status before swarm-manager is updated.

options.label: Log warning and keep returning StatusRunning (status quo with logging)
options.rationale: Add logging but keep current behavior. Relies on staleness detection (d2) to eventually catch stuck runs. Least disruptive but doesn't directly fix the root cause.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md with root cause analysis identifying 4 bugs, architecture diagram, key files, phased fix approach, scope boundaries, and test plan. Phases 1 and 3 are blocked on decisions d1 and d2 respectively.
